status: prepared, unpublished; arena outbox admission limit implemented
scope: The normal arena journal owner admits at most4096 pending result files; each new encoded receipt already has the1MiB recovery limit. This is a result-file admission bound, not a filesystem quota or player-capacity claim.

Opening the journal reconstructs only a file count in64-entry directory chunks. A preexisting backlog above the selected limit is preserved and replayable, not trimmed. The smaller constructor limit is used by isolated fixtures; normal server initialization retains4096.

Full admission returns a typed error without replacing or acknowledging existing results. Identical already-recorded retries remain possible at capacity; conflicting writes retain their conflict error.
Rename/removal update the owner's count before uncertain directory-sync acknowledgements. Repeated acknowledgement never releases another slot. Restart recounts the actual retained files.

The existing durable-before-release game path freezes an unrecorded decided outcome until capacity is recovered, then retries the exact outcome and releases/applies it once. No rating/reward arithmetic, token, class, wallet or scene policy changed.

checks.evidence: Full/identical/conflicting writes; reopened counts; duplicate acknowledgement; lowering capacity preserves the larger backlog.64 concurrent writers into8 slots produce exactly8 durable records and56 typed rejections. The actual game settlement hook writes to a real one-slot disk journal: a full journal preserves the earlier receipt and leaves the new match/profiles unreleased; freeing the slot permits the frozen result to record and settle once. Existing checksum/batch/synchronization/guild/weekly/shared-volume regressions pass.

limits: One live server/journal object owns writes and acknowledgements. This is not cross-process coordination, an external-editor quota or concurrent-backup/restore safety; pause writers before manipulating the volume and restart to recount after a restore.

The admission bound covers owned result files, not crash-temporary files, imported over-limit backlogs, all journals, database growth or other disk users. Operator disk monitoring/retention/recovery remain required.
A decided result held because its first journal write cannot succeed is still in memory, not crash durable. Holding players/profiles does not certify recovery through process loss before recording.

In-process race tests with actual disk receipts, not a latest connected binary, fresh Mongo outage, production/load check or complete1.72 security acceptance. Earlier direct Mongo/connected receipts retain their source scope; no unnecessary duplicate consumer/database run performed.

Account recovery remains an owner decision. A dependency-free one-time recovery-code option was proposed through the user question; no answer or implementation is assumed. Ordered1.71/1.72 publication remains open; accepted live is still1.70.0.
